text: S Korea firm aims to develop industrial-energy clusters in Vietnam

SK Group plans to establish its Southeast Asia regional headquarters in Hanoi, facilitating the expansion of its operations in the region, said Chairman and CEO of SK Innovation (South Korea), Mr. Choo Hyeong Wook.

During a meeting with Permanent Deputy Prime Minister Pham Gia Tuc on November 16, Mr. Choo said that the group aims to concentrate resources to develop Vietnam into a successful business model that can be replicated across Southeast Asia, contributing to Vietnam's socio-economic development.

According to the Group's leader, SK Innovation is collaborating with Vietnam Oil and Gas Power Corporation (PV Power) to implement the Quynh Lap LNG power plant project in Nghe An, aiming to ensure a stable energy supply to support Vietnam's economic development.
SK Innovation aspires to develop industrial-energy clusters in Vietnam, using energy infrastructure as a foundation to attract investment in new technology fields, particularly AI and data centers.
Developing projects under an integrated cluster model, rather than standalone investments, will create synergy and mutual support between energy infrastructure and technological activities.
The Quynh Lap LNG project could become the first model to implement this idea in Vietnam.

Mr. Choo said he expected that Vietnam will continue to improve policies to attract investment in new technology fields, including data-related regulations, creating favorable conditions for businesses to expand their investment activities.

Appreciating SK Group's interest and goodwill in investing in Vietnam over the past time, Permanent Deputy PM Tuc stated that Vietnam is renewing its growth model based on science, technology, and innovation, prioritizing the attraction of high-quality, environmentally friendly foreign investment projects that create significant added value.
Mr. Tuc hopes that SK Innovation will continue to expand its investment, especially in green energy, green growth, artificial intelligence (AI), and data centers.
According to the Permanent Deputy PM, ensuring energy supply is a crucial and urgent requirement to achieve annual double-digit economic growth from now until 2030.

Therefore, Vietnam prioritizes power projects capable of generating electricity before 2030, including the Quynh Lap LNG power project if SK Innovation and its partners can meet the implementation conditions.
Vietnam is currently moving towards developing a competitive electricity generation market, creating conditions for capable investors to operate effectively in Vietnam.

Regarding the development orientation of industrial-energy clusters, Permanent Deputy PM Tuc said that the Government supports the development of synchronized energy centers in line with the overall planning.
Accordingly, gas power plants should be located in conjunction with gas power centers and shared LNG storage infrastructure, rather than being dispersed across individual localities or enterprises.
The development of storage facilities must be calculated based on overall planning to avoid overlapping investments and resource waste.
Regarding the development orientation of energy centers associated with AI and data centers, Mr. Tuc emphasized the importance of ensuring a stable power supply for the operation of these centers.

The Permanent Deputy Prime Minister suggested that SK Group develop a comprehensive plan for the projects they intend to implement in Vietnam, clearly defining investment commitments and implementation timelines, serving as a basis for the Government and relevant agencies to coordinate in resolving arising issues and promoting project implementation.
